themes.label: UK-listed franchises broken up or taken private
themes.note: The London market keeps losing control of its own constituents to overseas and private capital, and the biggest live contest just resolved: Apollo's 715p-a-share, GBP5.7bn cash offer for easyJet is now a firm, board-recommended deal after Castlelake walked away under Rule 2.8 (ezj-apollo-takeover). Prologis has a recommended Rule 2.7 offer valuing Segro at ~GBP14.3bn that would remove one of the FTSE 100's largest REITs from the LSE (pld-sgro-takeover-bid), CD&R-owned OCS Group's agreed GBP3.1bn takeover will delist facilities-management leader Mitie entirely (ocs-mitie-acquisition), and AstraZeneca's exploratory ~$400bn approach to Bristol Myers Squibb would move the same pressure to the very top of the index (azn-bmy-merger-talks).

themes.label: Public-to-private buyout offers on listed companies
themes.note: Sponsor-, sovereign- and strategic-led buyouts keep pulling listed names off public markets, and two more landed this week: Nielsen will take DoubleVerify private at $13.60 a share in cash (dv-nielsen-acquisition) and Apollo's easyJet offer went firm (ezj-apollo-takeover), alongside KKR's signed $127-a-share agreement for Integer Holdings (itgr-kkr-takeover) and the completed $55bn PIF-Silver Lake-Affinity take-private of EA (ea-pif-consortium-take-private). Still unresolved: Grant Thornton and New Mountain Capital's $5bn deal for CBIZ runs a go-shop to August 27 (cbz-grant-thornton-acquisition), Pacific Equity Partners' SG Fleet vehicle bids A$3.60 a share for FleetPartners (fpr-sgfleet-takeover-bid), Steel Partners' $16.75-a-share bid for InMode is fought through both the Haifa court and the AGM ballot (inmd-steel-partners-buyout), EQT keeps raising for Perpetual (ppt-eqt-takeover-bid), Frasers Group's EUR38-a-share tender for Hugo Boss is unconditional (boss-frasers-takeover-offer), Stripe and Advent's $53bn offer for PayPal survives board rejection (pypl-stripe-advent-takeover-bid), Sazerac's ~$15bn approach for Brown-Forman has been rejected as not actionable (bfb-sazerac-takeover-bid), and ADW Capital's $18-a-share proposal for Driven Brands was dismissed as lacking a credible basis (drvn-adw-capital-takeover-bid).

themes.label: AI data-center capacity and power build-out
themes.note: Capital keeps pouring into the physical layer of AI compute, and the deals increasingly reach past the racks into the fuel and the fabric feeding them. Williams is paying up to $5.5bn for Momentum Midstream explicitly to connect Haynesville gas to Gulf Coast LNG and power demand (wmb-momentum-midstream-acquisition), while Prysmian pays ~$3.8bn for Atkore's conduit and cable-management business (atkr-prysmian-acquisition) and Everus bought modular electrical specialist Epsilon Industries (ecg-epsilon-acquisition). At the compute layer, Amazon's 2026 capex guide is up to ~$220bn with capacity constrained into 2027 (amzn-capex-raise-2026) and Alphabet's to as much as $205bn (googl-capex-raise-2026); Nvidia is in talks to backstop ~$250bn of financing for OpenAI's 10GW Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), has an equity-plus-Vera-Rubin pact with Safe Superintelligence (nvda-ssi-partnership), is scaling the $10bn Naver AI factory to 200MW with Brookfield capital (naver-nvda-ai-factory-partnership), and will co-design orbital compute payloads with SpaceX (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership). Orange and Morrison are building a EUR3bn, 400MW French JV (ora-morrison-datacenter-jv), Microsoft is deploying AMD Helios systems at scale (msft-amd-helios-partnership), NVIDIA prepaid $1.5bn for packaging capacity at Amkor (amkr-nvidia-packaging-partnership), Verizon signed a $1bn dark-fiber deal with Google (vz-google-fiber-partnership), Samsung agreed a ~$200bn memory and foundry MOU with Broadcom (samsungelec-avgo-chip-partnership), SK hynix has a long-term HBM pact with NVIDIA (skhynix-nvda-ai-partnership), and Doosan took control of Korea's sole wafer maker SK Siltron (doosan-sksiltron-acquisition).

themes.label: Chipmakers funding or locking in the customers that buy their chips
themes.note: Vendor financing and exclusivity remain the standard shape of frontier-AI deals, and both concentrate risk on the supplier's side of the trade: Nvidia is in talks to guarantee ~$250bn of lease and debt financing for OpenAI's Ohio campus (nvda-openai-datacenter-backstop), took a reported ~$5bn equity stake in pre-revenue Safe Superintelligence alongside a compute commitment (nvda-ssi-partnership), is buying ~4.5% of Naver via a ~$1bn share issue tied to a 200MW AI factory (naver-nvda-ai-factory-partnership), and has secured an exclusive commitment from SpaceX to build its AI infrastructure on NVIDIA platforms (spcx-nvda-starmind-partnership), while AMD is investing up to $5bn in Anthropic against a tens-of-billions MI450 purchase commitment (amd-anthropic-chip-partnership).

themes.label: Signed M&A deals hitting regulatory or legal roadblocks
themes.note: Deals investors thought were settled keep stalling in court, and the delay now has a price and a date: the signed, DOJ-cleared Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros. Discovery merger will not close until five days after a 12-day antitrust trial that a California federal judge has now set for March 2, 2027, with Paramount owing Warner holders ~$7m a day from September 30, 2026 in the meantime (psky-wbd-acquisition). InMode's special committee remains procedurally frozen pending the Haifa court's ruling on the competing buyout bids, with the fight also running through the AGM ballot (inmd-steel-partners-buyout).
